newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia slips but forestries bolster lively Helsinki.
newsitem.headline: Nokia slips but forestries bolster lively Helsinki.

text.p: Shares made another record close on Friday as recovery hopes boosted forestries to more than compensate for profit-taking in Nokia, brokers said.
The general HEX index rose 0.37 percent to the new 2,866.59 point record close in 903 million markka trade. Nokia fell 4.00 markka to 315.00, making up less than a third of volume.

Cyclical shares were catching up with others after recent signs that the economic fundamentals are sound, and UPM-Kymmene's LWC paper price hike and upbeat CEO comments reported on Friday sparked interest in forestries, brokers said.
"UPM's LWC price hike and recent upgrades by several overseas securities houses helped forestries," said one.
The forestry sector rose two percent and UPM added 2.10 markka to 104.00 in bumber 126 million markka volume.

Metals and mining group Outokumpu was boosted by steel maker Rautaruukki's 1996 earnings on Thursday and on an improving price outlook for metals, up 1.00 markka at 81.00 in heavy 47 million markka trade.

Better-than-expected earnings from beverage group Hartwall, data systems group TT Tieto and Interbank cheered sentiment and spread gains. Hartwall rose 3.00 markka to 227.00, Interbank jumped 14 percent and TT Tieto was up 2.00 at 418.00.
Finland's largest banking group Merita rose 0.30 markka to 18.00 in lively trade after Swedish rival SE-Banken's 1996 report confirmed the sector is on the rise in the Nordic region.
Next week's focus would be on more corporate earnings, Kemira on Monday, Metra on Wednesday and Partek on Thursday.
U.S. credit markets will be closed for President's Day holiday on Monday.
